points.text: PSI has no actual combustion experiments performed at lunar gravity (0.16 g); all statements about the Moon are theoretical bounds between microgravity and 1 g results.

The only lunar‑gravity analogue is the E‑FIELD flame study, which used an electric field to simulate reduced buoyancy, showing that lowering effective gravity makes flames more spherical and diffusion‑controlled.

In true microgravity (ISS cabin) flames are governed by forced ventilation and molecular diffusion, producing a spherical, low‑velocity diffusion flame; without buoyancy the flame would be even slower on the Moon, but exact numbers are unknown.

limitations: The PSI dataset contains no real lunar‑gravity fire tests; all lunar predictions are theoretical bounds or analogues. Results cannot be used for certification.
